title: HLS Progressive Runtime Boundary
problem: Nako's HLS planning and manifest model was mature, but the executable HLS runtime still waited for whole-output FFmpeg completion before publishing playlists and final artifacts.

evidence.summary: Opened the durable fearless refactor lane for making HLS runtime publication, playlist readiness, segment serving, artifact reconstruction, and playlist auth decoration future-ready.
Added an explicit HLS output publication policy in nako-transcode, preserving atomic VOD promotion while proving serve-visible running output with cleanup on cancel and failure.

Integrated serve-visible HLS output into server playlist paths so app and HTTP playlist requests return after playlist readiness while sessions remain running; generated segments serve, missing running segments conflict as not ready, and cancellation reaches Cancelled.
Moved HLS artifact reconstruction into nako-transcode via HlsArtifactSpec, letting the server rebuild manifests from a typed transcode boundary instead of local request-key substring parsing.
Consolidated HLS entry playlist authoring, session route binding, and browser/renderer auth query decoration behind a manifest-aware server playback boundary.

Ran final closeout gates, tightened running playlist readiness to reject partially written playlists without media or variant URI lines, and split LL-HLS, DASH/CMAF, DRM/key delivery, remote workers, selected-main-audio cleanup, and resource scheduling into follow-ons.

continue_policy.notes: HLS runtime publication and playlist readiness are progressive, artifact reconstruction is typed, and playlist auth decoration is manifest-aware. Open separate follow-ons for LL-HLS, DASH/CMAF, DRM/key delivery, remote transcode workers, selected-main-audio cleanup, or full resource scheduling.
